beats.beat: 'Specialty chemicals' here is a processing business, not a discovery business. The filing splits output into four groups: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM) and Hard Minerals (HM). The company treats mineral feedstock and sells the result to other manufacturers.

Sales reach the customer through a network the company does not own. The long-term arrangement with Corporate Promoter 20 Microns Limited is how the products are marketed, and the filing says the company derives substantial synergies from that promoter.

Operating footprint as disclosed: manufacturing at Plot 347, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat and Plot 104/3, Thenkasi Road, Pathur Village, Alangulam, Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu, plus administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur — and a third site, Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, whose licences are discussed later. None of these premises is owned by the company.

Contracts are not how the business is won. The filing states the company has entered into no long-term or definitive agreements with customers and instead relies on purchase orders to govern volume, pricing and other terms of sale.
Concentration is high. The top ten customers accounted for about 59%, 57% and 59% of revenue from operations in FY2015, FY2016 and FY2017 respectively.
Exports exist but are small and pinned to three countries: ₹1,068.18 lakh (₹10.68 crore) across the past five years, shipped to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka.

The filing summarises its own competitive position as six strengths — diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution, support of the holding company, product innovation and continuous R&D, and the management team. Read those as the company's account of itself; the R&D and management-team points appear on one page and the rest on another.

beats.beat: The filing reports six periods: the six months ended September 30, 2017, and five full years ended March 31, 2017, 2016, 2015, 2014 and 2013. The first of those is half a year, so it is not comparable line-for-line with the rest.

Profitability arrived late. Restated profit/(loss) after tax, in ₹ crore: FY2013 −0.27 (a ₹27.40 lakh loss), FY2014 −0.12 (₹12.17 lakh loss), FY2015 +1.50, FY2016 +0.90, FY2017 +1.75, and +1.33 for the six months to September 30, 2017.

The shape matters more than the level. Two loss years, then a jump, then a dip in FY2016 from ₹1.50 crore to ₹0.90 crore, then a recovery to ₹1.75 crore — a small business whose profit moves by lakhs either way.
Per share, restated basic earnings: −0.45 in FY2013, −0.20 in FY2014, 2.47 in FY2015, 1.46 in FY2016, 2.43 in FY2017 and 1.48 for the six months to September 30, 2017.

Cash from operations tells a different story from profit. Net cash inflow/(outflow) from operating activities, in ₹ crore: +2.01 (FY2013), +1.28 (FY2014), +4.22 (FY2015), +8.03 (FY2016), −3.50 (FY2017), +1.25 (six months to September 30, 2017). The FY2017 outflow is the year the filing flags in its own risk factors as a negative-cash-flow history.

Total restated assets, in ₹ crore: 30.19 (FY2013), 26.79 (FY2014), 25.93 (FY2015), 27.67 (FY2016), 32.74 (FY2017) and 34.25 at September 30, 2017. The balance sheet shrank for two years before growing again.

Missing from the supplied excerpts, and therefore not stated here: revenue from operations for any period, EBITDA, and the split between borrowed money and owners' money on the liabilities side. The excerpts contain asset totals but no debt line.

beats.beat: Four promoters are named: Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh and the corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited.

Pre-issue, the promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares, or 99.76% of paid-up capital, and the promoter group excluding promoters holds a further 21,510 shares, or 0.24%. There is effectively no outside shareholder today.

The capital structure at September 30, 2017: authorised share capital of ₹2,000.00 lakh (2,00,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each) and issued, subscribed and paid-up capital of ₹897.00 lakh (89,70,000 equity shares of ₹10 each). The gap between authorised and issued is the room the issue would use.

Related-party transactions are not hypothetical here. The filing states the company has entered into them in the past and may continue to, with disclosure under Accounting Standard 18 covering the last five financial years and the six months ended September 30, 2017.

Filings with the Registrar of Companies have slipped before: the filing records instances of non-filing, incorrect filing or delayed filing of statutory forms, in certain cases later filed with additional fees. It also records that certain statutory and regulatory licences, registrations and approvals have not been obtained for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara.

Litigation and other obligations: the company, its promoters, group company and directors are parties to legal proceedings; contingent liabilities and commitments not provided for aggregated ₹29.11 lakh as at September 30, 2017; the company does not own the premises housing two of its plants and its Bhuj and Udaipur offices; and it has not registered its corporate logo.

beats.beat: Specialty chemicals is a slice of a larger industry. CRISIL Research, cited in the filing, put the Indian chemicals industry excluding pharmaceuticals and fertilisers at ₹5,800–6,200 billion in fiscal 2017, with specialty chemicals other than agrochemicals and dyestuff at roughly 17% of that, or about ₹1,000 billion.
Growth: the specialty chemicals segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017, and the filing cites a CRISIL forecast of 12–14% CAGR going forward.

The end-markets inside that number are where a mineral processor's demand comes from. The filing gives separate CAGRs: construction chemicals, water chemicals and personal care ingredients at 15% each; surfactants at 13%; textile chemicals and flavours and fragrances at 12%; polymer additives at 10%.

Adjacent demand pools named in the filing: polymer demand is forecast to grow 9–10% CAGR between fiscals 2017 and 2020 and plastic products 11–13%; the domestic paints industry was estimated at ₹401 billion in fiscal 2017 and the organised cosmetics and toiletries market at ₹430–460 billion.

Structure: the industry is highly fragmented, with SMEs holding 70–75% market share, and only a few Indian players have the scale or capability to compete with global giants on product development and innovation.

Policy backdrop the filing leans on: a Draft National Chemical Policy aimed at raising the chemicals sector's share of GDP, industrial licensing done away with for most chemicals except a small list of hazardous ones, FDI permitted up to 100%, four approved Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions (Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Odisha) with about ₹9 trillion of proposed investment, and GST in force from July 1, 2017.

Headwinds the filing acknowledges. India's chemicals trade has run a deficit, with imports growing at 6.4% CAGR against exports at 6% between 2012-13 and 2016-17; exports to Europe face the REACH regulatory regime; and India's GDP grew 7.1% in fiscal 2017, with private consumption at 58% of GDP and urban population at about 31% in 2011 heading to 36% by 2020.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals processes and sells specialty chemicals — Functional Additives and Chemically Modified Minerals — and also processes and sells Soft Minerals and Hard Minerals. That is the whole business in one line: it buys and treats industrial minerals, then sells the output as inputs to other manufacturers.

The distribution model is the unusual bit. The company does not build its own sales channel: it has a long-term arrangement to market and sell through the network of its Corporate Promoter, 20 Microns Limited, and the filing lists 'support of our holding company' as one of its six strengths.
Scale: total restated assets were ₹3,424.96 lakh (₹34.25 crore) at September 30, 2017, and restated profit after tax for that six-month period was ₹132.75 lakh (₹1.33 crore).

On the offer itself, the supplied excerpts show the intended listing venue (the SME Platform of NSE, NSE EMERGE), the lead manager (Vivro Financial Services Private Limited) and the registrar (Link Intime India Private Limited). They do not contain the issue size, the price band, or the fresh-issue-versus-offer-for-sale split.
The shareholding context a reader needs before anything else: promoters held 89,48,270 shares, or 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.

intro.purpose: Orient a reader who has never heard of this company: what it makes, who it sells through, how small it is, and what the issue is — then say plainly what the excerpts do not disclose.

beats.beat: A company sells shares to the public in two ways at once: new shares it issues itself, whose proceeds go to the company, and existing shares sold by current owners, whose proceeds go to those owners. The excerpts supplied for this filing give the use of proceeds, which points to fresh capital, but not the split between the two.

The objects of the issue as named: to fund capital expenditure for setting up a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; general corporate purposes; and creating a public trading market for the equity shares by listing on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE) to enhance visibility and brand.

Two of those three objects are ordinary — a plant and working money. The third is worth pausing on: listing itself is listed as an object, which is normal for a company whose shares have no public market today, and it says the company expects the platform to do brand work as well as price discovery.
The intermediaries named: Vivro Financial Services Private Limited as lead manager and Link Intime India Private Limited as registrar.

Not disclosed in the supplied excerpts: the issue size, the price band, the number of shares on offer, the split between fresh issue and offer for sale, the identity of any selling shareholder, and the rupee amount allocated to each object. A reader should treat all six as open.

offer.heading: The offer and what the money is for
offer.purpose: State the objects of the issue and the named intermediaries, and state plainly which offer mechanics the supplied excerpts do not disclose.

beats.beat: Sales depend on a network the company does not control. Marketing runs through Corporate Promoter 20 Microns Limited under a long-term arrangement, and 'support of our holding company' is listed among the company's strengths — which is the same fact stated from the other side.

Nothing binds the customers or the suppliers. The filing says there are no long-term or definitive agreements with customers, with purchase orders governing volume and pricing, and separately that there are no such agreements with raw material suppliers, so timely supply at competitive prices is not contracted for.

Operating cash flow went negative in FY2017. The restated cash-flow statement shows an outflow of ₹349.75 lakh (₹3.50 crore) from operating activities that year, the only negative year among the six periods shown, and the filing lists negative cash flows in previous financial years as a risk in its own words.

One plant is running without the full set of approvals. The company states it has not yet obtained certain statutory and regulatory licences, registrations and approvals required to operate the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and that it cannot assure it will not be penalised for the non-compliance.

Revenue leans on a handful of buyers. The top ten customers accounted for about 59% of revenue from operations in FY2015, 57% in FY2016 and 59% in FY2017 — so the loss of a few accounts shows up directly in the top line.
